packets.text:
WASHINGTON — Secretary of State Marco Rubio has accused Ukraine of attacking ships carrying American-owned energy products in the Black Sea and urged Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky to find a way to end the bloody war.

“We have seen strikes on energy vessels in the Black Sea. And there’s been complaints, a lot, because we have American companies calling us and saying, ‘Hey, that was our oil on that ship that was hit by Ukraine,'” Rubio told Breitbart in an interview released Sunday.

“Now, I don’t believe Ukraine intentionally targeted them, but those ships got hit. And we already have a world that is facing an energy crisis,” he added. “We don’t need any exacerbating situations. And there’s been frustration that despite these asks, that has happened.”

Rubio also insisted Monday that the Trump administration has not paused intelligence-sharing meant to warn Kyiv of impending Russian ballistic missile attacks.

“I don’t know where he’s getting these things from or why he’s saying these things to the press,” Rubio told reporters in Uzbekistan in response to Zelensky’s latest complaint. “There’s been no pause. Zelensky should be focused on bringing an end to this war.”

Tensions between Washington and Kyiv have risen since President Trump’s Oct. 9 announcement that the US would import hundreds of thousands of gallons of diesel fuel in a bid to relieve prices at the pump.

During a call with Russian President Vladimir Putin that same day, the Kremlin tyrant suggested that he, Trump, and Chinese leader Xi Jinping sit down and come up with a way to end the brutal war, the Wall Street Journal reported Monday.

“I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine, and don’t want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table,” Trump posted on Truth Social Sunday amid bipartisan criticism of his handling of the war in Ukraine. “Great progress is being made.”

“Perhaps more importantly, Russia is doing very little, if anything, to help the Islamic Republic of Iran, compared to what they could be doing, and I want to keep it that way,” he added. “Zelensky is using Diesel Refineries in Russia as a target, knowing that these attacks are seriously hurting the world diesel markets, including those in the United States.”

On Friday, Trump halted plans to implement sanctions on Moscow under a bipartisan bill named in honor of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham (R-SC).

Meanwhile, Ukraine has insisted that its access to a military version of Elon Musk’s Starlink satellite system, known as Starshield, was throttled in systems moving faster than 100 miles per hour last week — preventing its air defenses from responding to Russian-launched, Iranian-made Shahed drones.

It remains unclear who ordered the apparent slowdown, with both Musk and the Trump administration denying responsibility.

Zelensky stressed over the weekend that US intelligence about Russian attcks isn’t replaceable.

“We have dozens of countries who help,” he told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” Sunday. “But only [the] United States has this unique intelligence to tell our side when Russia uses ballistic missiles. And we didn’t get it.”

With the Russian invasion of Ukraine set to mark its fifth anniversary in February of next year, Rubio said Monday that “no one’s winning that war.”

“This war is honestly about one part of Ukraine called Donetsk. The Russians occupy all but about 11% of that area in that province, Donetsk, or in that region of Donetsk,” Rubio told Breitbart. “The Ukrainians have a defensive line that they’ve embedded themselves in. They argue, and military strategists say is true, that it is the last defensible line. That if they give that up, there is nothing to defend Kyiv.”

“The Russians have not been able to advance in the battlefield and take that region … The United States remains willing, able, and prepared to play a mediating role if the opportunity presents itself to end this war through a negotiated settlement, which is how we think this war will ultimately end.”

packets.text:
The strikes were "probably not" deliberate, Rubio told Fox News in an interview.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio alleged that U.S.-linked oil infrastructure has been targeted in recent weeks by Ukraine amid its war with Russia during an interview with Fox News on Tuesday morning, though he conceded it was "probably not" deliberate.

Rubio, who attributed the recent rise in oil prices to conflict in the Black Sea between Russia and Ukraine as well as in Yemen with the Houthis, said in the interview that one of the U.S.'s concerns amid Russia's war was being unintentionally caught in the crosshairs.  

"The one thing we are concerned about, however, is that over the last few months, on a number of occasions, American-linked ships, American oil supplies have been targeted, probably not deliberately, but targeted nonetheless by Ukraine. And so that's something that needs to be addressed," Rubio said.

It was not immediately clear what specific incidents Rubio was referencing, though Ukraine has conducted strikes on the Russian Black Sea port Novorossiysk. The port contains export facilities for the Caspian Pipeline Consortium, which counts American oil giants Chevron and ExxonMobil among its top shareholders.

Ukrainian officials did not immediately respond to ABC News' request for comment about Rubio's claims.

The remarks came ahead of a meeting set to occur later on Tuesday between President Donald Trump and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly.  

Rubio told Fox News that the U.S. was enthusiastic about the concept of an energy infrastructure ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine, something Zelenskyy also called for on Monday.

"We think that would be a great idea, an energy infrastructure of cease fire, in which you're not- Ukraine's infrastructure is not being targeted. Russian energy supplies are not being targeted as well. It's an ideal outcome," Rubio said.

packets.text:
In brief: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Ukrainian forces repeatedly targeted vessels linked to the US, possibly unintentionally. Public reporting confirms that Washington previously asked Kyiv to avoid attacks on non-Russian tankers and infrastructure connected to US energy companies, but does not show that US-flagged or US-owned ships were repeatedly hit.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told Fox News on Tuesday,  Sept. 22, that Ukraine had repeatedly targeted vessels linked to the United States in recent months, probably unintentionally.
“Over the last few months, on a number of occasions, American-linked ships have been targeted, probably not deliberately, but targeted nonetheless by Ukraine. We can’t have that happen. That needs to be addressed,” he said.
Rubio did not publicly name the vessels or clarify whether they were American-owned, US-flagged or connected to the United States through cargo, chartering or energy infrastructure.
Rubio also backed a broader pause in attacks on energy infrastructure during the Fox News interview.
“We think that would be a great idea – an energy infrastructure ceasefire, in which Ukraine’s infrastructure is not being targeted, and Russian energy supplies are not being targeted as well,” he said
The claim appears to refer to vessels using Russia’s Black Sea ports to transport oil connected to the Caspian Pipeline Consortium, which carries Kazakh crude to export terminals.
The Financial Times reported in August that US Vice President JD Vance had asked Ukraine to halt strikes on tankers using the port of Novorossiysk. Washington was concerned that the attacks were disrupting global oil markets and affecting US companies, including Chevron and ExxonMobil.
According to the report, Ukraine agreed not to target CPC infrastructure or non-Russian vessels as long as those ships were not under Ukrainian sanctions and were not carrying Russian oil or other Russian cargo.
That means the vessels could be commercially connected to US interests without being US property. No publicly available report has established that Ukraine repeatedly struck ships sailing under the US flag or owned by US companies.
Ukraine has intensified attacks on Russian-linked shipping and oil infrastructure in the Black Sea and Sea of Azov in 2026.
Ukrainian forces have targeted Russian tankers, cargo ships and other vessels as part of an effort to disrupt Moscow’s energy revenues and military logistics. On Tuesday, the commander of Ukraine’s drone forces said his units struck 300 shadow fleet tankers ferrying Russian oil since July.
Reports confirm that Ukrainian strikes have affected vessels and infrastructure linked to Western energy companies, but no public evidence shows that US-owned or US-flagged ships were repeatedly hit.
Rubio’s comments come as Russia continues to target Ukrainian ports and civilian vessels in the Black Sea.
In an interview with Kyiv Post, Dmytro Barinov, head of the Ukrainian Ports Association, said Russian forces had damaged or destroyed more than 300 vessels since the start of the full-scale invasion. He said the attacks intensified in July, with Russian forces “hunting for vessels” entering or leaving Ukrainian ports.
Russia and Ukraine normally account for more than a quarter of global wheat exports, around two-thirds of sunflower oil shipments and about one-tenth of international corn trade.

packets.text: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has said vessels linked to the United States have repeatedly been targeted by Ukraine in recent months and that this cannot be allowed to continue. Source: Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty citing Marco Rubio on X (Twitter) Details: Speaking on Fox News on 22 September, Rubio said a so-called energy ceasefire in Ukraine, under which Russia would refrain from striking Ukrainian infrastructure and Ukraine would refrain from striking Russian infrastructure, is a good idea. He also said that, over the past several months, "on a number of occasions American-linked ships… have been targeted… by Ukraine", as had oil shipments. Rubio said the attacks had probably been not deliberate, but this is an issue that "needs to be addressed". Russia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio would meet in New York on 23 September. The US side neither confirmed nor denied that a meeting had been agreed, Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty reported. Background: Since July 2026, Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces (USF) have disabled 300 vessels belonging to Russia's so-called shadow fleet. Türkiye, meanwhile, is holding talks with Russia and Ukraine on the safe passage of grain ships through the Black Sea. Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said earlier that Ankara has developed a relevant plan. As of 23 July, inbound vessel traffic to Ukraine's Black Sea ports has been suspended due to the threat of Russian attacks. This followed weeks of air attacks on Ukrainian Black Sea ports. packets.text:
WASHINGTON -- President Donald Trump said that he has struck a deal to obtain diesel from Russia, a stunning reversal of years of U.S. pressure on Moscow over its war with Ukraine and an attempt to address high fuel prices ahead of the U.S. midterm elections.

Trump said on social media on Friday that he struck the deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin in a phone call in which he was expected to discuss a suspected case of plague in Russia. Instead, Trump announced that Russia will immediately supply more than 300,000 tons of diesel, followed by an additional 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons "immediately thereafter." Russia will deliver another 3 million tons "within a short period of time" after that, he wrote.

Trump's shocking announcement comes after he signed a sweeping Russia sanctions law last month that aimed at clamping down on Russia's energy economy, among other areas, that fuel its war against Ukraine.

His move casts doubt on the likelihood of the White House imposing sanctions on Russia this month, given that a bipartisan law passed by Congress directs the administration to target the top importers of Russian oil and gas.

Trump, in his announcement, did not address the sanctions or Russia's war but said, "Lower prices for Americans, especially our Great Farmers, Ranchers, and Truckers, is my Greatest Priority."

The White House did not immediately respond to questions about who was paying for the diesel from Russia and when the fuel being supplied under the agreement would become available. It also did not clarify whether subsequent supplies of Russian diesel set to come next month would be supplied prior to Election Day on Nov. 3.

Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev reposted the Treasury Department's announcement on X Friday and said that "Russia-US cooperation on diesel and energy will benefit the world."

The law Trump signed last month envisions sanctions on Russian officials, banks and a shadow fleet of tankers and bans all new U.S. investment in Russia and the handling of sovereign debt.

It also directed Trump to impose tariffs of up to 100% on the top five importers of Russian oil or natural gas, with an exception for countries that import less than 15% of Russia's natural gas exports and have taken significant steps to reduce those imports.

The U.S. has not imported Russian oil or gas since 2022, when the Biden administration banned them because of Moscow's invasion of Ukraine, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration.

Shortly after Trump made the announcement, the Treasury Department said it was immediately issuing a temporary license allowing Russian diesel to be supplied to the global market.

Gas prices globally have surged as the war in Iran upends the energy sector. The national average for a gallon of diesel in the U.S. was $6.23 on Friday, according to AAA, after hitting a record $6.52 on Sept. 22.
